title: Chapter 56
content:
Il-hyun clamped his mouth shut, glaring at the severed connection.

A full year had passed since he’d last laid eyes on that face. He hadn't expected a warm welcome, but catching the boy half-naked with an unfamiliar woman was an entirely unforeseen turn of events. Wetting his lips with the tip of his tongue, he methodically scrolled through the photo gallery on Wang Ryun's confiscated phone.

The burly man kneeling on the floor clearly shared a deep history with Lee Ja-kyeong. Most of the snapshots cataloged various high-caliber weapons and hardware, but nestled between the armaments were scattered photos of Ja-kyeong himself. Over the past twelve months, the boy’s skin had turned a golden sun-kissed tan, and unlike the rigid, wary facade he wore in Seoul, he was smiling with genuine, unfiltered radiance.

A smile he had never once offered to Kang Il-hyun.

Il-hyun’s thumb froze over the screen.

Beaming beside Ja-kyeong was the very same woman from the video call. Lowering the phone, Il-hyun walked over to where Wang Ryun was curled on the blood-slicked concrete, clutching his mangled hand. He grabbed a fistful of Ryun's hair, wrenching his head up.

"Who is she?"

Drenched in his own blood and gasping for air through broken breaths, Ryun glared at the photograph of Sasha before shifting his swollen eyes to Il-hyun.

"What is she to Lee Ja-kyeong?"

When Ryun clamped his jaw in stubborn silence, Il-hyun dangled the severed pinky finger right before his eyes.

"If you'd prefer to keep the rest of your fingers, you'd better start talking."

Ryun ground his molars together, spitting blood. "She's nobody."

"Hmm." Il-hyun narrowed his eyes into sharp slits. He resumed swiping through the gallery. The woman appeared in group shots with other residents, but there were no intimate portraits of just the two of them. Then why were they stripped down in a private bedroom? Thinking back, the girl had been wearing the straps of a bikini, but the sheer visual still set a dark, irrational fury boiling in his gut.

Tearing his glare from the screen, Il-hyun looked down at the battered man.

"Then what is your relationship to him?"

Ryun met the question with stony, defiant silence.

"His boss?"

Unlikely. The man's combat prowess was leagues below Ja-kyeong's. He had brute physical strength, but his knife work was sloppy and unrefined.

"We're brothers," Ryun growled.

Il-hyun let out a dry, incredulous scoff. "Brothers? Don't insult my intelligence."

"Don't fucking laugh," Ryun snapped back, coughing up crimson spit. "We are real brothers."

Scanning the man from head to toe, there wasn't a single shared physical trait between them. Il-hyun’s brow furrowed.

A stray memory surfaced—Ja-kyeong mentioning his past in fragments. How a man named Wang had pulled him from the gutter as a child, taking him to China to raise him as his own. How he had people who were closer to him than biological kin. Come to think of it, wasn't this bastard's name Wang Ryun?

As Il-hyun turned the pieces over in his mind, Ryun wheezed, his eyes burning with raw, protective hostility.

"Settle your score with me and finish it. Don't you dare lay a finger on my little brother."

The desperate, unyielding conviction in his voice was unmistakable. Il-hyun clicked his tongue, turning toward the doorway.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, Director."

Il-hyun casually tossed the severed knuckle into Tae-soo's open palm. "Take him to our private trauma clinic and have the surgeons stitch it back on."

"Sir?"

Tae-soo’s stoic eyes widened by a fraction of a millimeter. In all his years of service, he had watched his boss sever countless limbs, but ordering a severed digit reattached was a first.

While Tae-soo motioned for his men to fetch a sterile biohazard pouch and ice, Il-hyun dropped into a low crouch before Wang Ryun. He pulled a crisp silk handkerchief from his breast pocket, gently dabbing away the blood running down the man's forehead.

Ryun flinched, instinctively recoiling from the touch, only for Il-hyun to offer a dazzling, benevolent smile.

"You should have mentioned you were my brother-in-law from the start."

Ryun stared back in pure, unadulterated horror. When Il-hyun reached down to wipe the crimson from his chin, Ryun violently swatted the hand away. The bizarre, tender gesture sent a far more terrifying chill down his spine than having his finger bitten off.

What is wrong with this absolute lunatic? The man's easy, radiant grin made it impossible to tell whether he was genuinely pleased or contemplating another round of butchery.

Ryun had encountered every breed of syndicate monster in his life, but a creature like this was unprecedented. He finally understood why Lee Ja-kyeong had shuddered in disgust, cursing the man as a psychotic demon.

Moments later, the security detail hauled Ryun to his feet and escorted him to a waiting transport.

Left alone on the asphalt, Il-hyun looked down at the photograph on the phone once more. Seeing Ja-kyeong smile so brightly that his white teeth showed was a revelation. With Il-hyun, the boy had only ever offered strained, mechanical smirks or biting sneers.

During his initial months confined to a hospital bed, Il-hyun had sworn on his life that he would rip the operative to shreds the moment he dragged him back. Yet as the weeks bled into months, that thirst for simple execution had warped into something far more obsessive. Finding the boy had proven maddeningly difficult; the operative had slipped through every net without leaving a whisper of a digital footprint, fueling a desperate, gnawing paranoia. What if he slipped away forever?

Yet seeing him cornered with another woman today had reignited that murderous itch in his chest with terrifying clarity.

How should I even define this madness?

Il-hyun let out a low, ragged exhale, pocketed the phone, and strode toward his private sedan.

Well... I suppose I'll find out the moment I have that pretty face in front of me again. Whether I tear him apart... or do something else entirely.

"He told only you to fly to Tokyo?"

At Wang Han’s puzzled question, Jakyeong offered a curt, unhesitating nod.

He didn't need to ask why Wang Ryun had secretly slipped back into Seoul instead of staying in Japan—the man's long-term girlfriend had recently returned to Korea, and Ryun had undoubtedly crossed the border to see her. Unable to confess the brutal truth to Han, Jakyeong had fabricated a cover story about an urgent solo summons to Tokyo.

"Leaving me out of the loop?" Han pressed, crossing his arms.

"The Japanese syndicates specifically requested to vet me in person."

Ryun’s official assignment had been to negotiate with a heavyweight Yakuza clan, so claiming they had demanded a sit-down with their primary wet-work specialist was a plausible lie.

Han pouted, looking slightly offended at being bypassed, prompting Jakyeong to quickly smooth it over: "He probably figured it was better to leave you behind so you and Rita could enjoy some uninterrupted time together."

Han rubbed his chin, looking unconvinced, before deciding he needed to call Ryun to confirm. Jakyeong tried to wave him off, but Han had already dialed the number.

Fortunately, the encrypted line went straight to dead air.

Swallowing a quiet breath of relief, Jakyeong threw his essentials into a duffel bag.

"Did you secure a seat?"

"Managed to snag the last ticket on the red-eye."

"I'll drive you to the terminal."

"No need. I'll hail a cab out front."

Jakyeong forced a calm, reassuring smile to mask the frantic storm churning behind his ribs. His hands moved with ruthless speed, zipping the tactical compartments shut. The vivid memory of Kang Il-hyun’s demonic grin burned behind his eyelids; he needed to reach Seoul before that monster swallowed Wang Ryun whole. Knowing that unhinged psychopath, it was entirely within the realm of possibility.

"I really should have tagged along," Han grumbled, leaning against the door frame. "I could have gone for some authentic sushi and taken in the Tokyo skyline at night."

Jakyeong said nothing. Had he revealed the truth, Han would have barred him from leaving. When the three of them had first formed their operational cell, they had sworn a solemn pact: If one man's mistake marks the team for slaughter, the other two cut their losses and walk away clean.

Yet that rule was only spoken in theory; if the roles were reversed, Wang Han would have been the very first to march into the fire. Besides, this catastrophic mess was born entirely from Jakyeong's own failures. The responsibility rested on his shoulders alone.

I should have put the round straight through his skull that day instead of his legs.

Swallowing the bitter regret, he slung his pack over his shoulder. He had to reach Kang Il-hyun before the man laid another finger on Wang Ryun.

Following a grueling six-and-a-half-hour flight, the sweltering Korean summer air hit Jakyeong like a humid, suffocating wall—far heavier and stickier than the tropical breeze of Kuala Lumpur.

Because of the weekend rush, Incheon International Airport was packed to the brim with travelers. Slipping through customs under a clean foreign passport, Jakyeong hailed a taxi, directing the driver to an auto repair shop Wang Ryun had operated during their previous stay in Seoul.

Telling the driver to idle down the block, Jakyeong surveyed the perimeter. The garage was dark and deserted. He paid the fare, stepped onto the pavement, and approached the rusted side entrance. The shop had clearly been abandoned for months, layers of industrial grime coating the signage.

Slipping around back, he punched the six-digit override into the electronic keypad and slipped inside.

He flicked the breaker switch, the fluorescent tubes humming to life with a pale flicker. He tore open the concealed floor compartments beneath the tool benches, only to find the heavy weapons lockers completely bare. Ryun had systematically sanitized their primary cache before fleeing the country last year.

Rummaging through the secondary crawlspaces, he managed to scrounge up a tactical 12-gauge shotgun and a balanced trench dagger.

He slotted heavy buckshot shells into the tubular magazine, racked the action to chamber a round, and slipped out toward the detached corrugated shed in the alleyway. The steel roll-up door was secured with a heavy industrial padlock; Jakyeong leveled the shotgun, obliterating the shackle with a single blast, and hauled the shutter open.

Resting beneath a canvas tarp was the black motorcycle he’d ridden during his surveillance runs.

He retrieved the ignition key from a magnetic hide-a-box on the frame and activated his secondary tracking transceiver. As a fail-safe against black-site abductions, the cell had long ago embedded encrypted micro-beacons into the firmware of their primary burners. He hadn't imagined he would be using it under these circumstances.

The display initialized, overlaying a blinking red beacon across a satellite map of northern Gyeonggi Province.

Whether Ryun was currently in Kang Il-hyun’s direct custody was unknown, but Jakyeong prayed the man was still breathing. The signal was actively moving along a rural highway.

Kang Il-hyun had commanded him to report to his estate, but walking straight into the lion's den was tactical suicide. Facing overwhelming numbers on fortified ground was a death sentence; intercepting the target in transit was the only viable play.

Jakyeong pulled the full-face helmet on, snapping the visor down.

Wheeling the heavy bike into the alley, fat raindrops began splattering against the concrete.

Fucking perfect. Even the sky is working against me.

He kicked the starter, the engine roaring to life with an aggressive rumble, and peeled out into the deluge. The motorcycle sliced through the downpour, weaving aggressively between highway traffic as he pinned the throttle wide open.

After forty minutes of relentless riding, the tracking coordinates narrowed to a localized radius. The route led straight toward the winding mountain passes approaching Kang Il-hyun’s private estate.

Through the sheets of rain, a familiar silhouette emerged up ahead: a heavy, black corporate sedan with pitch-black window tint.

It was unmistakably Il-hyun's security vehicle.

Jakyeong eased off the throttle, trailing the vehicle from a discreet distance until the road narrowed into an isolated, forested mountain stretch devoid of civilian traffic. Dropping a gear, he surged forward, roaring past the sedan and executing a sharp, sliding drift across the asphalt, blocking the entire single-lane road.

The sedan slammed its brakes with a deafening screech, coming to an abrupt halt barely ten feet from his front tire.

Jakyeong kicked the kickstand down, dismounted, and yanked his helmet off in a fluid motion.

He drew the 12-gauge shotgun from the scabbard on his back, racked the heavy slide, disengaged the safety, and leveled the barrel dead-center at the driver-side windshield.

Torrential rain poured over his head, soaking his dark hair and plastering the strands across his forehead as icy streams cascaded down his brow and jawline.

Behind the sweeping rhythm of the windshield wipers, the black sedan sat completely motionless in the rain.
